incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: redis-main-usw2 maxclients reached (95% of limit)
incident-bot: keys: redis-main-usw2, shard: 3, metric: connected_clients, value: 480 (limit=500)
incident-bot: linking PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD12345

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: #PD12345 fired -> severity: high. Notifying on-call schedule.

maya (oncall): acked the page. I'm looking. seeing 5xx errors on /v1/llm/generate in SLO dashboard. rolling numbers around 22:03 UTC.

chris (sre): on it. Any recent deploys to api or background jobs?

maya (oncall): there was a canary earlier from platform job "cache-warm" at 21:58. also autoscale didn't trigger for redis for some reason.

sam (platform): i pushed the cache-warm canary but it was supposed to be rate-limited. looking at job logs now.

lei (prod): customer reports: several tenants seeing 500+ latency and token generation failures. support ticket count +7. marking P1 potential.

chris (sre): pulling redis info:
```
$ redis-cli -h redis-main-usw2 INFO clients | egrep "connected_clients|maxclients"
connected_clients:482
maxclients:500
```

chris (sre): client list shows many ephemeral connections from service 'batch-warm' at identical time windows. suspect bug in backoff.

maya (oncall): can we temp throttle that job? sam, can you pause the cache-warm rollout?

sam (platform): pausing rollout now. command: `kubectl scale deployment cache-warm --replicas=0 -n infra`

sam (platform): paused. traffic to redis from that job dropped to ~0 in the last 20s.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD12345 acknowledged by maya (oncall). Escalation timer 15m.

chris (sre): added immediate mitigation: increased maxclients on redis by editing `/etc/redis/redis.conf` to bump `maxclients 1000` and restarted redis on primary to pick up setting. Restart was rolling, no master failover.

chris (sre): restart logs:
```
[22:12:05] saving to disk...
[22:12:09] configuration reloaded, maxclients=1000
```

maya (oncall): after bump and pausing warm job, errors on /v1/llm/generate dropped from 18% -> 1.5% in 3min. latency back to normal for most tenants.

lei (prod): customer impact: 7 support tickets, 3 timed-out requests for queued enterprise customers during 21:58-22:11 UTC. no data loss, only transient request failures. Tentative severity: P2 now.

chris (sre): follow-ups:
- root cause: cache-warm rollout lacked exponential backoff and created a connection surge (ephemeral sockets) when combined with existing bursty traffic.
- mitigations implemented: paused rollout, increased maxclients, rolled config change.
- short-term: add IP-based rate-limits on batch nodes, enforce backoff on cache-warm.
- medium-term: enable prefix/KV caching on gateway to reduce unnecessary redis hits, and make autoscaler for redis reactive to connected_clients metric.

maya (oncall): handing off to chris for postmortem. i'll clear the page after we confirm all systems stable.
